text: A corner booth, two menus nobody opens. {client} talks about everything except the reason for the dinner — the new director, the weather, somebody's divorce. The real subject sits under the table, waiting.

reads.unreadable: Whatever is eating at them stays wrapped in anecdotes. You cannot find the thread.
reads.likely: There is a want under the small talk — money, rest, respect, you cannot tell which yet.
reads.clear: You can hear the real subject circling: it is their {need}, and it has been hungry for a while.
reads.certain: It is {need} — you knew before the bread arrived. Every anecdote tonight has been about it, in disguise.

choices.label: Ask straight out what they need
Acknowledge the strain before they name it

text: Halfway through the second course the anecdotes align, and you see the pattern: this dinner is about their {need}. You say it out loud, gently, before they have to.

choices.label: Now talk about what you can actually do

text: "I know this year has taken more than it gave," you say, and {client} puts down the fork. The armor comes off one buckle at a time. What is underneath is a want with a name: {need}.

choices.label: Put something real on the table

text: Finally {client} says it — half sideways, wrapped in a joke that is not one: "I need to know what I am working toward." The want underneath has a name: {need}.
The table is quiet now. Whatever you say next will be remembered word for word — this is the part of the dinner that becomes the contract behind the contract.

choices.label: Promise the lead — twelve months, your word
Promise a prestige picture — eighteen months
Promise a real break — six months, protected
Promise a serious fee jump — twelve months
Be honest: you cannot promise that right now

text: {client} looks at you for a long second, then nods — the slow nod people give when they decide to believe you one more time. The promise now has a date, and dates in this town are witnesses.

effects.text: Expectation talk with {client}: a concrete promise, with a deadline.

text: You talk about pipelines and timing and the market — fluently enough that it sounds like a plan instead of a postponement. {client} accepts it. For now. The word 'now' is doing real work in that sentence.

effects.text: Expectation talk with {client}: bought time, promised nothing.

text: The stalling shows its seams by dessert. {client} smiles the professional smile and asks for the check — the one gesture that says: noted, and filed.

effects.text: Expectation talk with {client}: the evasion was heard as exactly that.

text: "I can't promise you that right now. I won't pretend I can." It is not the answer {client} wanted — but it is the first sentence all evening they fully believe. Honesty pays into a different account, at a slower rate.

effects.text: Expectation talk with {client}: no promise, but the truth.
